title: Honest Bands for the Entire Dose-Floor Gain Curve under Vanishing Design Density
banked_reason: Stage 0.5 BELOW NOVELTY FLOOR: tier=subfield < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 7.1 < 7.4; math and decision referees pass, salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: The result is confined to fixed finite strata, known smoothness and thinning exponents, a polynomial density envelope, and reporting horizons above the stated lower cutoff, making it a specialized benchmark rather than a broadly deployable LMTP procedure.

The claimed observable construction remains difficult to reproduce because its Gram thresholds, bias multiplier, small-sample cutoff, and other constants are specified only existentially rather than as executable numerical choices.
The software and clinical significance remains motivational, with no implemented band or applied demonstration to establish practical usability.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 produced a matched-order honest gain-band frontier, a total upper-band construction, a same-class lower bound, and a faithful transfer from the accepted pointwise parent; the D0.5 math and decision referees passed, and the parent theorem was attested verbatim from its accepted paper source. The field-tier claim fell on the cold general review: the delivered scope is a specialized subfield benchmark, with existential calibration constants and no implementation or application. A sharp constant, unknown-exponent adaptation, and below-cutoff phase theory remain separate research questions.
tldr: Exact dose floors create a moving atom at the threshold, while subtracting the natural-course value cancels the regression level and exposes a boundary-slope regime. The minimax expected maximum width of one finite-sample \(90\%\)-honest band for the entire gain curve on every public horizon \([0,\Delta_n]\) has order \(r_n=\Delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\min\{1,\Delta_n/h_n\}\), where \(h_n\) solves \(nh_n^{2\beta+1}(\Delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=\log(e+\Delta_n/h_n)\). An exhaustive midpoint-Voronoi partition of the moving local-polynomial cells, class-based bias envelopes, and finite local confidence allocation give one total measurable upper band; the same-class two-law and separated-bump experiments give the matching all-band lower bound. The observable curve equals the causal exact-floor gain under the simultaneous latent-response lift \(Y(a)=g_X(a,U)\), \(A\perp U\mid X\), consistency, and continuity of the structural response mean.
gap: Published work separately provides pointwise exact-clamp inference; joint asymptotic simultaneous inference for a stochastic threshold intervention on a finite grid, with grids growing toward a compact threshold set and bands obtained by interpolation; weighted uniform regression rates under vanishing design density; and generic bias-aware intervals. It does not state a finite-sample honest band under polynomial thinning with matched expected-maximum-width lower bound for the deterministic exact-clamp gain curve.
fill: The project derives the exact gain identity, defines the continuum entropy root and its transition, constructs one total band with explicit bias and design-failure control, and proves an all-band lower bound by a named band-to-testing reduction and a same-class two-law-to-packing bridge.
